brand.intro: A cash-pay practice built by a facial plastic surgeon who sold his first practice, regretted it, and started over. Esthetics Center is where Alpha began.

practice.headline: Medicine first. Culture first. Then growth.
body: Dr. Reginald Rice trained in facial plastic surgery in the early 1990s, when Botox was used only for eyelid spasms and the only filler on the market was made from cow collagen. After the Great Recession pushed him to sell his first practice to a hospital system, he and his wife sold assets and started again about thirty minutes away, with no insurance contracts and everything on the line.

It was still one location with one physician, one nurse and one aesthetician when his son-in-law, John Wheeler, joined to work on the practice rather than in it. A few hard early hires set the rule that still holds: culture first. John set the goal of the biggest med spa in the country. Reg added the condition: the biggest and the best.

headline.text: We saw a bad way to have it done, and we knew we could do it better.

body.text: One of the most powerful things that I personally have gotten from doing this platform and partnering with other practices is the fact that every perspective is different and has value.
If I look back at my surgical career, I think one of the biggest mistakes that I have made was not spending more time in other people's operating rooms.

quote.text: I've always maintained that aesthetic medicine is medicine first.

founders.name: Reginald Rice
bio: A facial plastic surgeon who completed his fellowship in 1995, Dr. Rice has watched aesthetics grow from surgery alone to the field it is now. He built Esthetics Center as a cash-pay practice after selling his first practice to a hospital system, a decision he would not make again.

He co-founded Esthetics Center's management company with his son-in-law, John Wheeler, and is Alpha's founding partner. His share of the vision has always been the second half of it: not just the biggest, the best.

line.text: We have a doctor patient relationship that is truly sacred, even though it is aesthetic in its designs and its outcomes.
So I think that's when the stake was pounded in the ground that we were going to make culture first our first priority.
Because I didn't want it to just be the biggest.

quotes.text: But we've done literally millions, tens of millions of dollars of business out of that tiny little room.
If I only knew then what I know now, I would not have done that.

milestones: Founding partner of Alpha Aesthetics Partners.

story: The original Esthetics Center. For four years the patient care coordinator worked from a windowless room barely bigger than a closet while the treatment rooms grew around it, and the team did tens of millions of dollars of business from that room. A recent expansion finally gave the front of house its own space and gave the aesthetician rooms the quiet they needed.

flags: Webflow says est. 2018, but the first employee has been with Dr. Rice 17 years in El Dorado Hills. Confirm the founding year.
Brand is still unannounced (never launched); content is ready for when it is.

brand.intro: Holden Timeless Beauty is Dr. Amanda Holden's San Diego County practice: an emergency physician's precision inside rooms built to feel like a vacation.

practice.headline: Built for San Diegans, by one.
body: Dr. Amanda Holden was a single mom in medical school who chose emergency medicine over surgery to stay close to her kids. In 2017 she opened a single room, injecting friends and family, then trained the emergency providers she had worked beside. They became the HTB glam squad.

Every location is designed around the five senses: Miami Beach chill on the speakers, a signature scent, bubble blue treatment rooms with chandeliers overhead, a Coronado Bridge painting and a bathroom styled like a nightclub. HTB also stands for have the best and hold time back.

headline.text: Alpha is such a great choice in so many ways because it gives you autonomy.

body.text: They care so much about your team and ensure that your team will be safe, protected, happy, have a future of opportunities and possibilities in the future, and they're just so supportive.
When you have an autonomous partnership like Alpha, you keep your brand entirely unique.
body.source: Dr. Amanda Holden, founder interview (Amanda Conclude) 00:05:07

quote.text: We've really created a brand that anytime you go to any other location, you still feel like you're here at headquarters.

founders.name: Amanda Holden
bio: A board certified emergency physician who has lived in San Diego since she was nine, Dr. Holden learned the business of aesthetics from a physician who ran fifteen clinics across Southern California, then trained with injectors across the country.

She has studied every side of the business since, from people and finance to marketing, and leads HTB as its visionary alongside an integrator who runs clinical operations. Her goal is to reach 33 million people through the practice, the stage and the teams she trains.

line.text: One of the first pillars is to dream bigger than you ever thought possible.
Even if you have skills, it's very hard to run a business.
The team matters the most.

quotes.text: It's fun in here. It's welcoming.
We built HTB for San Diego, and we didn't wanna lose any part of our brand representation, brand identity with any sort of partnership.
quotes.source: Dr. Amanda Holden, founder interview (Amanda Conclude) 00:06:35

milestones: Founds Holden Timeless Beauty in a single room.

story: HTB's headquarters and the fullest version of the brand: bubble blue treatment rooms, chandeliers to look up at mid-treatment, custom lip signs on the walls and a graffiti bathroom that reads got lips, hold time back.

flags: Amanda lists Oceanside as a location; Webflow has Carlsbad. Which is current?
La Jolla is closed and is not mentioned anywhere.

brand.intro: Refined Aesthetics is Sarah Safa's non-surgical practice in a restored building in historic downtown Leesburg, where education comes before any treatment.

practice.headline: Educate first. Say no when it's right.
body: Sarah Safa, a board certified physician assistant trained in plastic and reconstructive surgery, spent years watching surgeons treat the non-surgical side as an afterthought. About ten years ago she opened Refined Aesthetics on her own to give it full attention, and demand from Northern Virginia, DC and Maryland soon brought an office manager, then more injectors.

Every consultation is complimentary, and the team is as comfortable saying no as yes. Patients range from young Arlington professionals to Middleburg horse country, and more men walk through the door here than at most practices in the region.

headline.text: Since partnering with Alpha, I sleep at night.

body.text: I had the right backing and the right people behind me in my corner working for me, not me working for them in order to make those dreams come true.
This is my baby here at this company, and I knew that they were gonna allow me to take care of it.

quote.text: What I cared about is that every single person in my chair felt like they were getting the education that they deserved and a better understanding of what was available to them.

founders.name: Sarah Safa
bio: A Virginia native, born in Charlottesville and raised outside Richmond, Sarah planned on orthopedics until an elective rotation in plastic surgery out of PA school. Eighteen years later she still calls aesthetics happy medicine.
She is also an educator, teaching colleagues across the country and writing on where the field is going. Her team travels as far as Brazil and Canada to learn treatments before they reach the US.

line.text: It was a passion of mine, and it really gave me the ability to practice what I like to say is happy medicine.
Passion for people, passion for your purpose.
We also equally have no problem telling patients no either.

quotes.text: For me, it was a no brainer.
I just knew that I would be able to take this risk without taking risk, if that makes sense.

story: Refined Aesthetics sits in a restored historic building in downtown Leesburg, chosen because, in Sarah's words, the heart of Loudoun County lives in its historic town. The renovation is the point: an old building made new, the way the team wants patients to feel walking out. A second floor, which the team calls the penthouse, opened after the partnership with Alpha.

quote.text: We might be aging in our years, but we want you to feel like you've been refurbished.

milestones: Opened the second floor, the penthouse: more providers, more services.

flags: Founding year: Webflow says 2015; Sarah said eight years ago (2024) and ten years ago (follow-up). Confirm.
Penthouse opening date not given.
The building name sounded like 'the Tolbert Building'; not used until confirmed.

brand.intro: The Laser Center of Marin has been a Corte Madera fixture since 2003: a family-built practice known for the NorCal natural look.

practice.headline: The NorCal natural look, for twenty years.
body: Kevin and Denise Jones opened the Laser Center of Marin in 2003, after Kevin's twenty years in Silicon Valley tech and Denise's thirty years as a hospital nurse practitioner. Kevin and their son built out the treatment rooms themselves, their daughter ran the front desk, and Denise's siblings answered phones and stocked shelves.

It started with laser hair removal and IPL. Injectables came a couple of years later and are now the bigger part of the business. Some of the team have been here more than fifteen years, and some patients have seen the same provider for just as long.

headline.text: They basically said, you do what you do well.

body.text: That meant keeping our name, keeping our culture, keeping our personnel in place
They really came from the same background we did, almost about the same timeframe with their original locations, and we saw that family environment, we saw that very similar culture to ours

quote.text: The culture of Marin County is about healthy, what we call the NorCal natural look.

founders.name: Kevin Jones
founders.headline: Co-founder
bio: Kevin spent twenty years in Silicon Valley telecom before an IPL treatment of his own sent him looking at aesthetic technology. He studied the franchise models, decided he could do it better on his own, and built a higher-end practice in a class A building in Corte Madera.

quotes.text: It was more than just employee relationship, it was a family relationship.
I think the biggest difference is it's a people business versus a machine business

milestones: Co-founds the Laser Center of Marin.

founders.name: Denise Jones
founders.headline: Co-founder
bio: A Marin native and nurse practitioner who spent thirty years at a large hospital, Denise brought the medicine to the practice while Kevin ran the business. She named it, too: The Laser Center, TLC, tender loving care.

quotes.text: It's the most beautiful place in all the world.
It was really a family oriented start.

milestones: Co-founds the Laser Center of Marin.

story: A class A building in Corte Madera that Kevin and his son built out by hand. Marin patients live outdoors and know how to look after their skin, and they come for results that look rested, never overdone.

flags: Kevin and Denise are no longer involved; their founder records are set to former. Confirm you want them shown.

brand.intro: The Williams Center in Latham, New York is four centers of excellence under one roof, built by facial plastic surgeon Dr. Edwin Williams as a destination practice beside the Albany airport.

practice.headline: A destination practice, by design.
body: Dr. Edwin Williams opened his practice about thirty years ago, when cosmetic dermatology was not yet a phrase and facial plastics meant surgery. His plan was to bring specialists together, each staying in their lane. When a hospital partnership stalled in bureaucracy, he built it himself, at 38, next to the airport, so patients from out of town could fly straight in.

Today it is four centers: facial plastic and reconstructive surgery, hair restoration at Saratoga Hair Transplant Center, non-surgical aesthetics, and an accredited surgery center on site. Half or more of the patients come from out of town.

headline.text: When they first came here to talk to me, they did a lot more listening than they did talking

body.text: I wanna make sure we're taking care of our family as we grow with the Alpha family.
If we have a successful business model, okay, why would we break that model?

quote.text: My real big vision from the very beginning was to build a destination practice.

founders.name: Edwin F. Williams
bio: A facial plastic surgeon for three decades and past president of the American Academy of Facial Plastic and Reconstructive Surgery, Dr. Williams still does the facelift surgery he teaches. He insists his surgeons speak at the meetings they attend.

His fellowship, approved when he was 38, is one of about sixty in the country and now takes two fellows a year from roughly fifty applicants. The Williams Center is a family business, too: his daughter and son-in-law work there, alongside staff who have been with him since the 1990s.

line.text: My goal and focus and what we're kind of obsessed with is truly best in class for each of the different specialties.
If you take good care of people and you treat them like family, they just keep coming back.
If we're gonna call ourselves leaders, we need to walk the walk.
I look at having fellows kind of like having children

quotes.text: I can't do surgery forever, but I can share and teach a lot of the things that I've learned over the past many years.
We're only as good as our succession.

milestones: President, American Academy of Facial Plastic and Reconstructive Surgery, 2015 to 2016.

story: Built by Dr. Williams at 38 beside Albany International Airport so patients could fly in for surgery in the on-site surgery center. It is a family business in a family town: Albany, not Manhattan, where people put down roots and the same patients come back for decades.

quote.text: What makes Albany different is it's not Manhattan. It's not a big, big city, and it is much more of a family oriented town. We grew a family business here.

story: Saratoga Hair Transplant Center, part of the Williams Center since 2015, led by a double board certified facial plastic surgeon who is in the room from the first graft to the last.

flags: Founding year: Webflow says 1992; Dr. Williams said about thirty-one years ago. Confirm.
Fellow count differs between interviews (23 or 24 vs almost 30). Neither is used.
Surgeon names left out on purpose (poaching).

brand.intro: Anne Therese Aesthetic Medicine is a physician-led practice in Columbus, Ohio and Southwest Florida, founded in 2004 by former ER doctor Dr. Anne Therese Stubbs.

practice.headline: A medical practice that feels like a spa.
body: After ten years as an ER physician, Dr. Anne Therese Stubbs took a course in Canada, saw what a laser could do for sun damage, and went all in. In 2004 she left emergency medicine with no business background. A year practicing inside a Columbus mega salon taught her hospitality. The lesson she kept: patients, not clients, deserve both.

The practice has been early to most of what worked: the first Fraxel in Ohio, the first SmartLipo in Ohio, the first EMSculpt in Columbus, and a 38-foot Beauty Coach that pulled up outside the headquarters of Columbus's retail brands. Ohio patients wintering on the Gulf Coast followed her south, and the Florida practice grew from there.

headline.text: This is not Dr. Anne's retirement plan. This is Dr. Anne's growth plan.
headline.source: Dr. Anne Therese Stubbs, founder interview (atam1) 00:21:31

body.text: What made Alpha different is John Wheeler, number one.
body.source: Dr. Anne Therese Stubbs, founder interview (atam2) 00:03:20

body.text: We're part of something bigger. We're part of something better because everybody who's in it, all the partners, are the top of the top, the creme de la creme.
body.source: Dr. Anne Therese Stubbs, founder interview (atam2) 00:04:02

quote.text: We wanna look good, and we wanna look great for our age, but we don't want anybody to know what we did.
quote.source: Dr. Anne Therese Stubbs, founder interview (atam1) 00:11:31

founders.name: Anne Therese Stubbs
bio: Trained in emergency medicine and trauma, Dr. Stubbs ran a very large ER before leaving for aesthetics in 2004. She came in from outside the four core specialties the industry once took seriously, and built a practice that outlasted the skeptics.
Her nurses train at her side, over and over, until they know the anatomy cold. Approached by about eight private equity firms in two years, she chose Alpha.

line.text: I didn't want clients. I wanted patients.
line.source: Dr. Anne Therese Stubbs, founder interview (atam1) 00:10:14

line.text: It had to be hook, line, sinker.
line.source: Dr. Anne Therese Stubbs, founder interview (atam1) 00:04:39

line.text: To be good at something, you have to do it more than one day a week.
line.source: Dr. Anne Therese Stubbs, founder interview (atam1) 00:16:13

quotes.text: I didn't really know much about business, but I knew how I wanted patients to be treated.
quotes.source: Dr. Anne Therese Stubbs, founder interview (atam1) 00:06:19

quotes.text: We've always been growing, and we're not gonna stop now.
quotes.source: Dr. Anne Therese Stubbs, founder interview (atam1) 00:21:31

milestones: Leaves emergency medicine and founds the practice.

story: Columbus South. Ohio patients who winter on the Gulf Coast followed Dr. Stubbs down, then sent their friends, and the Florida practice grew from there. Patients here want it all, now, and more men come through the door than in Columbus.

quote.text: I always call that area Columbus South.
quote.source: Dr. Anne Therese Stubbs, founder interview (atam1) 00:13:23

flags: Transcript writes 'doctor Ann'; quote uses Dr. Anne. Confirm the spelling she uses.
Columbus-area locations (Gahanna, Lewis Center): no place detail in the interview.

brand.intro: RN Esthetics is one of New England's first nurse-owned and operated aesthetics practices, founded in 2012 on Boston's North Shore.

practice.headline: Nurses should be doing aesthetic medicine.
body: Michelle Doran was a surgical nurse, then a nurse practitioner in primary and palliative care, where she learned that time with a patient matters most. In 2012 she and fellow nurse Linda started RN Esthetics as a side gig in two rooms, with Michelle's mom at the front desk. A year later it was named Best of the North Shore, and it has won every year since.
Lynnfield came first, then Salem in 2017 and Newburyport in 2019. The team works in scrubs, as a team, with no commissions, so a recommendation is only ever about what the patient needs.

headline.text: Partnership and collaboration is important to growth and to provide opportunity for our team members, and I didn't wanna wait on that.

body.text: I love having the colleagues and the Alpha network, working with the marketing team, the financial piece, taking that off my plate, HR, etcetera, and letting me focus on what I love, which is clinical.
The big thing expanding is having a financial backer because prior opening our locations, I've had to sign personal guarantees and go to small banks and really finance the project myself.

quote.text: Nurses historically have been the most trusted profession year after year.

founders.name: Michelle Doran
bio: A nurse practitioner for more than twenty years, Michelle was steered toward the profession by her father, a tax consultant who noticed his NP clients were the happiest people he saw. She trained in Botox and fillers while still in primary care and practiced at day spas before there were medical spas.

She co-founded RN Esthetics to show what nurse-led aesthetics could be, and she is passionate about the standards the field still lacks: ongoing education, clinical proficiency and treatments delivered as medicine.

line.text: You're not worrying about the insurance and the fifteen minute visits.
I think it's that we're down to earth.
We are not pushy. We don't work on a commission.

quotes.text: We didn't want to have a business. We just wanted to do what we loved, and it grew from there.
My mom would work the desk for us, which was funny.

milestones: First Best of the North Shore.

story: Where RN Esthetics began in 2012, in a historic space Michelle still calls beautiful: two rooms, two nurses and Michelle's mom at the front desk.
Opened in 2017. After partnering with Alpha, Salem expanded within the same building with new treatment rooms, and took in the providers and patients of Seaside Aesthetics in Marblehead.
milestones: Expanded within the building; Seaside Aesthetics joins.

story: A small satellite in 2019 that rounded out the North Shore, now in a larger space in town.

Susan Goldberg opened Seaside Aesthetics in Marblehead in October 2015, a second career after twenty-five years giving anesthesia. She built it as a place where women would be cared for in mind, body and spirit. When it was time to step back, she wanted her patients in safe hands, and Seaside's providers and patients joined RN Esthetics in Salem.

quote.text: What I mean by happy medicine is that when you make people look better, they feel better, and their self esteem is better.

flags: Salem expansion and the larger Newburyport space: dates not given.
Team counts from the interview (8 RNs, 6 NPs, 8 estheticians) are dated; not used. Add to Team by role if current.

brand.intro: Dontage is Waseem Garbia's practice in Fairfax, Virginia, built on reading each face for what it is and enhancing it, not changing it.

practice.headline: Don't age, with a little French accent.
body: Waseem Garbia has been a PA for more than twenty years, across surgery, critical cardiology and emergency medicine. He first injected Botox in 2002, when training meant half a day with a coworker, and turned an eye for faces in three dimensions into a career teaching other injectors.

In 2018 he moved from North Carolina to Northern Virginia to be near family and opened Dontage without a patient to his name. One of the most diverse and transient regions in the country suits him: every culture reads beauty differently, and the work starts with each patient's own anatomy.

headline.text: Sometimes you need a whole bunch of superheroes to change the world.

body.text: Alpha lets me be my own individual. They let me be me, and they actually encourage that.
They're not trying to fit me in a box, they're not trying to tell me to do something their way or the highway, they're not making this cookie cutter, and they're not making it a med spa chain.

quote.text: It's definitely an art form. It's definitely medicine.

founders.name: Waseem Garbia
bio: Waseem came to aesthetics from surgery, cardiology and the ER, and learned it the hard way, on the job, before there were training centers. He has been teaching other injectors ever since, and holds nothing back.
He opened Dontage in 2018 after deciding it would be easier to build his own practice than to keep building someone else's.

line.text: We don't want to really change anyone, we just want to enhance what they have.
I'm not going to hide any of my knowledge.
It's definitely an art form. It's definitely medicine.

quotes.text: In 2018, I founded Dontage because I decided that it would be easier for me to build a practice of my own than actually help someone else build their practice.
I want you to have all the resources that I can't give you.

story: Dontage opened in 2018 and has since moved to a larger space nearby. Northern Virginia is one of the most transient regions in the country. Waseem stayed, for his family and for the mix of cultures that walks through the door.

quote.text: Virginia is a transient community, which I call home, because I love how diverse it is

flags: Founding year: Webflow says 2012; Waseem said 2018 (after hesitating on 2017). Confirm.
Surname spelling (Garbia) taken from Webflow.

brand.intro: InBloom Health + Medispa in Londonderry, New Hampshire is Dr. Tanya Lawson's integrative practice: wellness inside, aesthetics outside.

practice.headline: Inner and outer wellness, under one roof.
body: Dr. Tanya Lawson graduated from the Canadian College of Naturopathic Medicine in 2006 and ran two integrative medical centers and a medical spa in Canada. She bought her first device, an IPL, in 2007, after patients who felt better told her they wanted to look better too.

In 2013 she moved to New Hampshire for a fresh start, where the bank offered her a $500 credit card and nobody knew her name. She took locum work, rented a room in a group clinic, then opened InBloom in a single room with the restroom down the hall. Within three years, through COVID, it doubled to nearly 4,000 square feet.

quote.text: It's not it can't be done, it's how can it be done, and let's do it.

founders.name: Dr. Tanya Lawson
bio: A naturopathic doctor who built her first practices in rural Canada, Dr. Lawson spent her first year in the US as a hospital consultant, which confirmed she belonged in private practice. The idea for InBloom came to her there: people growing into the best version of themselves.

She built a community from scratch in New Hampshire, through the local moms' club and volunteer work she still does, and runs InBloom as a place of support rather than competition, for patients and staff alike.

line.text: Never giving up. Right? You have obstacles. Life is obstacles.
I wanna grow things. I wanna help people. I wanna empower people.
I want everyone on my team to feel supported, empowered, and really to grow into their full potential.

quotes.text: I also didn't realize your credit score doesn't follow you when you move countries.
I think it really confirmed for me that private practice is where my heart is.

milestones: Graduates, Canadian College of Naturopathic Medicine.

story: InBloom began in one room with one waiting room and a restroom down the hall. The current Londonderry office is almost 4,000 square feet, doubled within three years and through COVID, and every color and finish was chosen to feel like a place of hope for patients and staff alike.

quote.text: Even when we choose our colors, our decor, we want it to feel positive, uplifting, a place of hope, not just for our patients but our staff.

flags: No Why Alpha in this transcript (it cuts off at 24 minutes). Why Alpha section left empty.
Founding year: Webflow says 2011, but she moved to the US in 2013. Confirm InBloom's opening year.

brand.intro: Flawless Med Spa + Wellness is Heather Badal's Albuquerque practice, built on a simple motto: you are already flawless.

practice.headline: A med spa of the people, for the people.
body: Heather Badal studied art history, earned an MBA, spent eleven years at Intel, where she built its first supplier diversity program, and ran a mobile lithotripsy company with her husband serving rural hospitals across New Mexico and Colorado. When physicians started asking about aesthetics, she opened Flawless at 42, about fourteen years ago.

It sits in a strip mall and feels like a New York gallery, hung with abstract art so no one is told what beauty should look like. The team was rebuilt after COVID and has stayed together since. Staff are bilingual, consents come in Spanish, and patients fly in on private jets and walk across the border.

quote.text: When I opened Flawless, I had this motto. And the motto is, you are already flawless. We just help you stay that way.

headline.text: So when I think about partnership, I think about collaboration.

body.text: When I started FLAWLESS, I started it with this idea of beauty for the people.
So when we brought our staffs together, it's like the joining of two families.

founders.name: Heather Badal
bio: Born and raised in Albuquerque, Heather left for Boston University and the wider world, then took a first job that required her to move home. It turned out to be a blessing: the city is in her soul.

She founded Flawless as a businesswoman, not a provider, and sees the practice as a collective of providers, staff and patients. One of the children she was raising when she opened it now helps run it.

line.text: Aesthetics is an art form. And our nurse injectors are true artists.
Everyone is welcome here.
My vision is that we are with you through your life because your skin is going to change through your life.

quotes.text: I used to think when I opened the doors initially that Flawless was me, but now Flawless is a fraction of me.
These lines that I have on my face, it's because I've learned a lot. You know, I've cried, I've laughed, and I've learned so much.
he is the OG. He's the original.

flags: Bair Medical tuck-in copy from bair1 + fl2-4. Doctor's surname spelled Bair to match the brand; the transcript renders it Baer/Bear, confirm.

story: Bair Medical Spa opened in Albuquerque in 2004, started by Dr. Dean Bair's wife, a children's advocate attorney, while he practiced family and sports medicine. It outgrew its first office, moved within the same building, and built its own home in 2008.
Dr. Bair trained injectors for Allergan and Galderma and sat on Allergan's medical advisory board. Joining Flawless brought the two teams together, and gave Flawless its first full-time physician.

quote.text: When I talked to John, I felt immediately I can trust this guy, and that that was more important than the numbers or anything.

brand.intro: Mint + Needle is Brandi Gregge's Delaware practice, in Middletown and in a restored historic jail and firehouse in Lewes.

practice.headline: Look your best. Feel your best. Be your best.
body: Brandi Gregge grew up in California with very little and a mother who told her to look her best, feel her best and be her best. She came east for the University of Pennsylvania, became a nurse practitioner in primary care, and began training in aesthetics in 2014, slowly and on purpose, because she sees it as a specialty of medicine.

She opened Mint + Needle in Middletown in 2019. Needle for what she does, mint for calm and for home by the water. The second location, in Lewes, is a historic building that was the first jail and firehouse in the first city in the first state, renovated with the original bars still in place.

headline.text: I wanted to partner with a company that wanted to partner with me.

body.text: For example, Mint and Needle is partnered with Alpha, but Mint and Needle is Mint and Needle.
When you have a true partnership, you're not competing with each other. You guys are all growing together into the same direction.

quote.text: To me, it's industry versus specialty, and this is a specialty, and people are trying to turn it into an industry.

founders.name: Brandi Gregge
bio: A nurse practitioner who also holds an MBA, Brandi took her time coming into aesthetics: years of study and evidence-based training before she opened her own practice. She spent eighteen months talking with Alpha and came to PartnerCon before she signed.
She credits where she is to hard work and to the people she surrounds herself with, and now to a team she trusts to treat every patient like family.

line.text: It is a specialty of medicine, and I think that we're starting to lose that piece.
I really wanted to have a foundation to be not just a good provider but be a great provider based off of evidence based practice.
I'm always going to outwork. I will always keep pushing.

quotes.text: We choose our reality, and we do that every day with every single decision.
They're good people. They're just good people.

story: A historic building in Lewes that served as the first jail and firehouse in the first city in the first state, fully renovated with a modern Nantucket-meets-Lewes charm and the original jail bars kept in place. Unlike many beach towns, most of Lewes lives here year-round, which is why the Mint + Needle way fits.
The original Mint + Needle, opened in 2019. Delaware's small-town loyalty to small business, and its reach, an hour to Philadelphia and two to DC and New York, made it home.

flags: Lewes opening date: 'about a year and a half ago' at interview. Confirm the year for the milestone.

brand.intro: Privé Med Spa in Lexington, Kentucky was opened in 2011 by PA Brandice Harrison and banker Becky McDonald, four months after they met.

practice.headline: Named for a time when nobody talked about it.
body: Brandice Harrison started as a PA in surgery and emergency medicine in Eastern Kentucky, then took a job at a small Lexington med spa answering phones and scrubbing floors because the work made her happy. When the owner needed another injector, she asked Brandice to learn. Becky McDonald was a senior vice president of operations at a bank. A mutual friend introduced them in July 2011, Becky resigned in August, and Privé opened on November 1.

Privé is French for private, because in 2011 nobody talked about Botox. Brandice owns the medicine and the brand, Becky the business, and the goal has not changed: you, only rested. Brandice also trains injectors nationally for Allergan Aesthetics.

headline.text: Honestly, to be something better than we already are.

body.text: For me personally, what it means for me operationally is to have a support system for my role, which I have not had in fourteen years.
I wanted to be part of a team, if I'm honest, that is moving and advancing the needle, no pun intended, in the right direction in aesthetics.

bio: A PA since 2001, Brandice spent years in surgery and emergency medicine in a part of Kentucky where nobody knew what a PA was. She prayed for direction, took a front desk job at a med spa, and found what she calls the happy side of medicine.
She runs the clinical side of Privé with her husband, the practice's medical director, and travels nationally as a trainer for Allergan Aesthetics, bringing every new technique home to her team.

brand.intro: LexRx is Alexa Nicholls Costa's Boston aesthetics practice: neighborhood clinics, an injector training program, and a team of fourteen women.

practice.headline: Drybar meets SoulCycle, in your neighborhood.
body: Alexa had the idea in 2012 and launched in 2015 as a concierge practice, then rented a room by the hour on Newbury Street. Beacon Hill, on Charles Street, became the first brick and mortar. South Boston followed in 2019, then Nantucket in 2020.

In 2018 she started Inject With Lex, a training program that later partnered with Boston College and supplied her first two hires. LexRx runs clinics, education and medical directorship under one roof, and the first person she hired is still on the team.

brand.intro: Preva Aesthetics began as one room in Denver and now runs in Denver and Encinitas: preventative aesthetics, natural results.

practice.headline: Started in one room in Denver. Renamed for prevention. Built to go further.
body: Preva opened on January 1, 2022 as Skin Den, one 100 square foot room in Denver, staffed by people hired for their energy as much as their skill, several of them from the fitness world. That May, Michelle renamed it for what it stands for: preventative aesthetics, natural results, and a name that could travel.

Today it runs in Denver and in Encinitas, opened largely by Denver team members who moved west. New injectors train for at least two to three months before their first basic treatment, and every opening draws more than 300 applications.
